article_manifest.title: Mali: about forty civilians killed Sunday by armed men in the Ménaka region
article_manifest.original_title: Mali: une quarantaine de civils tués dimanche par des hommes armés dans la région de Ménaka
article_manifest.summary: Published on: Advertisement In Mali, the Executive Office of the Idaksahak community expressed Monday "its strong emotion and immense dismay" after the death of 48 civilians of the community, last Sunday, on the side of Tagadayat, in the Ménaka region According to their statement, "these defenceless civilian populations were attacked by armed elements of Daesh [Islamic State group, editor's note], arrived on board several motorcycles".

article_manifest.title: Gunmen Kill 40 Civilians in Mali
article_manifest.original_title: Gunmen Kill 40 Civilians in Mali
article_manifest.summary: More than 40 civilians have been killed in attacks on settlements in Mali’s northeastern Menaka region, with security and community sources reporting that armed men targeted camps over the weekend. The attackers, reportedly travelling on motorcycles, raided several camps largely inhabited by members of the Daoussahak community. The community’s executive bureau blamed the Islamic State group for the killings.

article_manifest.summary: While in Geneva, Switzerland, as part of the 77th session of the Executive Committee of the Programme of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), the Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralization, Government Spokesperson, Brigadier General Issa Ousmane COULIBALY, chaired the ceremony to celebrate the 66th anniversary of Mali's independence on October 17, 2026 The ceremony took place in the presence of Mali's Ambassador to Switzerland Sékou dit Gaoussou CISSE, surrounded by his counterparts from Burkina Faso and Niger, as well as members of the Malian community based in Geneva.

article_manifest.title: Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger Resume Talks with ECOWAS
article_manifest.original_title: Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger Resume Talks with ECOWAS
article_manifest.summary: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger have reopened formal discussions with the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS), more than 18 months after leaving the regional organisation. The two sides agreed on Saturday to set up joint working groups to develop a framework for future cooperation, signalling renewed efforts to rebuild relations. The three countries, governed by military juntas, withdrew from ECOWAS in January 2025 after establishing the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), following military coups and growing disagreements with the regional bloc.

article_manifest.title: Fight against drugs in Niamey: 461 people arrested around schools and on the Niger River
article_manifest.original_title: Lutte contre la drogue à Niamey : 461 personnes interpellées autour des écoles et sur le fleuve Niger
article_manifest.summary: A total of 461 people, including 50 minors, were arrested in Niamey during an anti-drug operation conducted on Saturday, October 17, 2026 by OCRTIS and the other Internal Security Forces. Dubbed "Back to school without drugs", this operation allowed the seizure of 7,250 tramadol tablets, as well as diazepam and several quantities of cannabis. The operation took place in two simultaneous phases .

article_manifest.original_title: Opération Dougoukoloko : les FAMa frappent deux positions de groupes armés à Ménaka et Douentza

On Saturday, October 17, a base housing armed elements as well as war and logistics equipment was located about 65 km southwest of Menaka, thanks to intelligence.

article_manifest.title: Fighting insecurity: FAMa strike at the heart of terrorist networks in the centre and north of the country
article_manifest.original_title: Lutte contre l’insécurité : Les FAMa frappent au cœur des réseaux terroristes dans le centre et le nord du pays
article_manifest.summary: The General Staff of the Armed Forces informs the national opinion that the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are continuing the permanent operations of surveillance, control and security of the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko . On Saturday, October 17, 2026, the exploitation of precise intelligence made it possible to locate, 65 km southwest of the city of Menaka, a large base housing several terrorist elements as well as war and logistics equipment.

article_manifest.title: Report: 'Indiscriminate' drone strikes by Malian and Russian 'Africa Corps' forces
article_manifest.original_title: تقرير: ضربات "عشوائية" بالمسيرات نفذتها قوات مالي و"فيلق أفريقيا" الروسي
article_manifest.summary: Summary Data from the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project, a US-based conflict observatory, showed that Malian and Africa Corps forces carried out 47 drone strikes that killed 94 civilians between April and August, up from 22 strikes that killed 44 civilians a year earlier . Human Rights Watch said in a report today, Monday, that the armed forces in Mali and its Russian supporters carried out drone strikes in an apparently "indiscriminate" manner, and committed other violations as part of an intensive attack against militants and separatists during the past months, killing dozens of civilians.
